chat.text:
> When is the live transcription actually sent to you, the smart assistant?

**How it works now**
- Both assistants hear the same lines. The fast assistant doesn't hand anything to me. It only answers quickly, then stays quiet.
- I'm not woken per sentence. Your lines are batched and reach me when you pause, ask something, speak to me by name, or six sentences pile up. The last line of each batch says which: `(paused 6 s)`, `(asked)`, `(6 sentences)`, or `(the mic went off)`.
- That batching is the delay you felt. Typed lines arrive after a short moment.
- Lines dictated before your refresh most likely stayed in the page's buffer and were never posted to the session. I can't confirm that from here.

**Showing it in the UI**
- I don't know of a marker in the dictate UI today that shows when a line goes to me. This is a dictation change, so `mastermind-dictation-2` owns it.
- I asked you a question on your prompt: do you want a "sent to smart assistant" marker on each dictated line? Say yes and I'll pass it to that mastermind.

sections.heading: ↩️ Moving a chat card for reference

items.text: No need to design this first since it's not what's being worked on right now — just noting it in case it didn't make it into the system yet.

**Prompt class:** it lives in `core/Task/Prompt.js`. Every card in your session file is written as a `Prompt`, but Chat v2 doesn't use that class and keeps its own copy.

**What I did**
- I filed a task for context cards and the Question class.
- I sent your points to `mastermind-dictation-2`: topic cards holding questions and tasks, one refinement driving both V1 and V2, and a Question that extends Task and stays open until you accept the answer.
- A cheap agent is checking past work on the Question class and on how prompts, replies, questions and tasks are logged. I'll relay what it finds.

chat.text: Why would chat to not use that class and keep its own copy?

I don't know the reason, and I haven't seen the history. My guess is that Chat v2 was built quickly in a separate pass without wiring in the shared class. The plan already fixes this: step 3 puts V1 and V2 on one reader built from the real `Prompt` class. The copy is what caused the checkbox bug.

The Question class already exists, so nobody needs to build it.

```
core/Task/Question.js   extends Task
  open -> answered -> complete   (complete = owner has read the answer)
core/Task/Prompt.js     extends Task
  raw[], paragraphs[{id,text}], sentences (computed: a1, a2...),
  replies[{id,text,by,anchor}], refined, notes, parts
session.jsonl           one list of tasks; replies and answers live ON
                        what they answer (prompt.replies, question.answer)
```

- **Question completion:** an answered question completes when the owner reads the answer, which matches your rule.
- **Log shape:** the session holds one list of items, and replies and answers sit on what they answer. That is your 2026-10-25 decision, documented in `dictation-debug/chat-shape.md`.

So the remaining work is getting V1 and V2 to use these classes, and drawing question widgets and cards.

⬜ How the prompt renders as chat bubbles and groups needs a solid look — it's probably different between V1 and V2, and the two need to be unified

When a question is asked it should be upgraded into its own question card — a little question icon block, created the same way a task is — and the answer gets added to it when it comes in; questions need to be referenceable

A question is created inside the context block currently being worked in — a context block is like a chat bubble you can put things into, made for whatever's being discussed, and titled as part of the refinement process
Whatever topic is being talked about shows on screen, a new topic appears when you switch, and a question goes to the root if it doesn't belong to a topic or into that topic's block if it does

This isn't critical for dictation specifically right now, but getting these conversation cards working matters — adapting live to what's said, merging each clean sentence into its card (e.g. a question sentence gets associated with the question card)
A Question class should extend Task — though check whether that's right for the dictation mastermind first, since this was already discussed yesterday
Question can extend Task because both share the same completion idea: a question isn't complete until it's answered
A question should stay incomplete until its answer is accepted, not just given — asking means not understanding yet, and unanswered questions need to keep resurfacing until satisfied
⬜ Launch a secondary agent to build the Question class, but generalize it so any kind of card — question, statement, task, etc. — can be created the same way

p-1792965434620.title: Routing for clickable cards in the global sheet
p-1792965434620.text: Chat should be the same code as the session detail page. Cards click through to a detail view (preview card -> full render, swapping the chat area, with a way back). Reload must keep the spot. The global sheet cannot own the URL path (site navigation must keep working). Options: no routing (UI-only state), a query-string variable, or the existing router on a session's own page. No new elaborate routing system.

add.title: Spawn fresh child agents; stop reviving old sessions
add.description: Reviving an old session (mastermind-dictation-2, parented to vscode-mastermind) credits its cost and task completion to the old parent. Write the rule in system docs: start fresh sub-sessions of this session, revive only in rare cases; masterminds must document state so a fresh one can resume. Audit that every task asked for in this chat is attributed to this session and completed.

p-1792965565590.title: Fresh sessions, not revived ones (accounting)
p-1792965565590.text: Reviving old agents misattributes cost and task completion to the original parent. Document: spawn fresh child sessions; masterminds keep state documented. Audit that all tasks asked in this chat are counted under this session and get completed.

p-1792966091101.title: Converge outcomes; fast=place, smart=title/restructure
p-1792966091101.text: V1 compact, V2 cards rich but lists not rendered as lists. One data structure for both. Fast assistant: place each sentence (and turn questions into Question items) and stop; smart assistant: titles and restructuring, reliably. Show live raw whisper in V2. > Does the smart assistant tail the fast assistant's work?

No. I'm woken by batches of your raw lines (a 12 s pause, a question, my name, or 6 sentences), not by each sentence the fast assistant places. Waking me on each placed sentence is possible, and you said the token cost is fine. I've asked `mastermind-dictation-2` what wires that and what it would take.

The rest went to `mastermind-dictation-2` as asks and is logged on your prompt:
- **Roles:** the fast assistant places each sentence and turns questions into Question items. I write titles and restructure.
- **Live text:** V2 shows the live raw whisper text.
- **Cards:** refined cards converge into ranked outcomes and open decisions instead of growing.
- **Lists:** numbered lists render as real lists.
- **Timeout:** it checks whether the send-after-pause timeout should come down.

> Do we use the Session class server side, and can a session tail its own log?

From a quick code check, which I haven't double-checked:

- **Session class:** yes, Servex uses the framework's Session class (`core/Session/Session.js:18`). `Servex/agents/Agents.js:65` registers resolvers on it, so it runs server side too and isn't only a browser view.
- **Tailing:** the existing follow tool (`Servex/Follow.js`) already accepts voice sessions. Follow delivers new lines of a `session.jsonl` into an agent's inbox, and the agent reads them with `updates()` (`Servex/agents/External.js:120-135`). The file watch is on the server, not the browser dev socket.
- **Consequence:** I can tail my own `session.jsonl` today with `follow` and `updates()`. That means no new transport, which fits what you asked for. The change is to swap my wake rules (12 s pause, question, name, 6 sentences) for follow.

No, it isn't limited to one task, and nothing in the code enforces that. The name only says what it was started for. In `roles.js` it's just a `mastermind` with no path, so it can work on whatever you give it. That's why the name is confusing: it suggests a task link that doesn't exist.

A mastermind named for its job and its folder is clearer, such as `mastermind-chat` at `public/framework/ux/Dictate`. The docs fix already asked for covers that, and the two running ones keep their current names until they finish.
